standout_why: I compared against the Anker F3800 and F3800 Plus pages (ChatGPT results 1–2), which state Anker's own 11–165 V input range and that its 240 V output can't run while the unit charges from 120 V AC. ChatGPT also had Jackery 5000 Plus pages and manuals. None of these covers the Apex 300, OSCAL or Growatt sets. None says that Anker's US store shows the F3800 Plus, ChatGPT's 'Best overall' at $2,999.99, as Sold Out today. None says that Growatt's HELIOS 3600 has no 240 V outlet unless you buy two units and a $139 hub. I could not extract text from the Anker design-guide PDF (results 9–10), so I can't rule out that it covers Anker's own input window. Its standout is 2, not 3, because the voltage-window fact only decides the set if the page picks the Apex 300.
kit_items: 240 V power station: BLUETTI Apex 300. One unit has a NEMA 14-50R at 120/240 V, but total AC output is capped at 3,840 W (StorageReview). It is in an approved store (awin:bluetti_us). Alternatives: OSCAL PowerMax 6000 (6,000 W, 120/240 V, $1,659.99), or 2× Growatt HELIOS 3600 plus the Double Voltage Power Hub.
Expansion battery: BLUETTI B300K (2,764.8 Wh). BLUETTI sells it in bundles with the Apex 300.
Solar charge controller: BLUETTI SolarX 4K (500 V Voc, 4,000 W). You need it for high-voltage panel strings, because the Apex 300's own inputs stop at 60 VDC.
Solar panels: BLUETTI 200 W / 350 W / 500 W panels from BLUETTI's own bundles. Wire them so each string's Voc stays at or below 60 V on the built-in inputs, or use the SolarX 4K for longer strings.
Home connection: a 14-50 or L14-30 cord to an inlet box and a transfer switch or interlock, installed by an electrician. I sourced no product for this.
OSCAL alternative: PowerMax 6000 + PM400 SE 400 W kit, $1,969.98 from OSCAL. It is the cheapest 240 V set in an approved store, but I could not confirm its solar input window.
